thesis: DexCom (Nasdaq: DXCM) makes continuous glucose monitors (G7, Stelo). Q3 2026 revenue 1,344.5M (+11%; US +14%, international +5%), GAAP operating margin 24.3% (+420bp), FY2026 revenue guide 5.20-5.25B with margin guidance raised. TTM revenue about 5.10B, operating income 1.22B, FCF about 1.10B. At 80.35 (2026-11-11 close) market cap is about 29.97B, EV about 29.4B: about 30x TTM GAAP earnings, 5.8x revenue, 3.7% FCF yield. Net cash about 0.57B after the 1.25B 0.375% 2028 convertible (conversion 162.41, no maturity before May 2028); undrawn 200M revolver. Quality is high; price assumes durable low-teens growth and margin gains. Not shown to be mispriced.
counterthesis: Growth is decelerating to 11% with international only +5%; distributor channel is 85% of revenue so a few distributors matter; securities class action, derivative actions and G6/G7 class action are unquantified; 9M OCF fell to 1,120M from 1,147M while buybacks ran 1.0B, so buybacks outpace cash generation and cash fell; net income comparisons include non-operating items; competitive (Abbott) and reimbursement risk not examined; stock fell from 88.48 (11-04) to 80.35 despite a raised margin guide, cause not established.
invalidation: Revenue growth below 8%, operating margin guidance cut, adverse ruling in the G6/G7 litigation, loss of a major distributor or payer coverage, or evidence that the type 2 non-insulin expansion (NEJM CONNECT trial) is not converting to volume.
